title: Cold-path batching playback
next_steps: Alex to share raw throughput CSV and heatmap by 2025-11-03
Customer to run 3rd microbench with fixed seed traffic by 2025-11-05
Schedule canary day with production traffic slice (TBD week of 11/10)
action_items: Alex: export detailed per-route latency histogram and attach to CRM (2025-11-03)
Jamal: propose batch size & concurrency matrix for cold-path scenarios (2025-11-04)
Maria: validate data residency requirements with legal and confirm retention window (2025-11-06)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on cold path latency and continuous batching behavior. We validated steady-state numbers but saw two cold-path spikes caused by KV cache misses and container spin-up. Agreed to run a deterministics microbench and adjust batching/concurrency matrix; Redwood to provide heatmap and recommended playbook for cold-start smoothing.
questions: What counts as cold path in customer traffic?
How will model slices be routed under burst?
Can we keep sub-100ms tail for most user flows?
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-28 15:00 UTC, duration 45m, attendees listed above.

00:00 Alex Morgan: okay thanks everyone for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, we're gonna do a quick sync on the cold-path batching playback, revalidate the numbers from last week and decide the next runs.
00:12 Maria Gonzalez: yeah thanks Alex, we only have 45 minutes so I'll be brief. We saw two spikes in the last 36 hours where some sessions hit 800ms tail — most normal requests are around 120-170ms.
00:26 Jamal Rivera: interesting, can you share the trace ids? was that more queuing or container spin-up?
00:33 Tom Becker: i pulled a few traces — looks like KV cache miss + pod spin, there's a 200ms gap then another 400ms while model starts warm state. our autoscaler is set to 0 minimum for cost reasons, so there is a cold VM/POD path.
00:52 Alex Morgan: okay that's helpful. to set context: Redwood's continuous batching will try to aggregate requests but if the pod isn't there, we see headroom loss. we have two levers: increase minimal idle capacity (dedicated or reserved), or reduce cold path latency via priming / pre-warm.
01:10 Ibrahim Khan: can you clarify priming? is that something you do server-side or we trigger?
01:17 Jamal Rivera: both. priming can be an internal warmup (short synthetic requests to keep model loaded) or you can have a tiny dedicated pool that handles cold starts. there's also KV cache priming to avoid prefix misses.
01:34 Rachel Lee: we've got about 15% of traffic that's truly cold (new user sessions). for those flows, this tail matters. for product success we want <=250ms 95th for main path.
01:47 Alex Morgan: got it. our goal then is: keep 95th <=250ms for main path, and reduce cold path spikes to below 500ms if possible.
01:56 Maria Gonzalez: timeline question — how soon could we see improvements from config-only changes vs infra changes?
02:03 Jamal Rivera: config-only (batching + concurrency tuning, priming scripts) can help in days. infra (min replicas, dedicated GPUs) will take procurement/approval and could take weeks.
02:18 Tom Becker: procurement is fast if it's reserved capacity within Redwood Dedicated, but legal sign-off for Private VPC will take longer.
02:25 Alex Morgan: okay so short term: try tuning continuous batching parameters, propose concurrency targets that avoid queue overfill but keep throughput. long term: discuss dedicated pool or guaranteed warm pool.
02:37 Maria Gonzalez: can we look at the specific batch sizes that were used? we saw variance between 4 and 24 depending on concurrency.
02:44 Jamal Rivera: yes i ran a couple of afternoon runs — when concurrency hit 12 we started seeing longer q delays; batch size growth was sudden because many requests accumulated.
02:56 Jamal Rivera: note: the instrumentation in your agent uses an older sdk so some per-batch labels are absent — that, plus transcription — i mean metric gaps — makes exact correlation fuzzy.
03:12 Alex Morgan: understood. action: i'll export the per-request CSV and a batch-formation heatmap (time vs batch size vs latency).
03:21 Ibrahim Khan: we also want to capture token length variability; some payloads are much larger.
03:28 Jamal Rivera: yes token distribution matters; we saw long tails when token length > 800. continuous batching heuristics can be tuned by token cap & timeout.
03:40 Maria Gonzalez: is there a simple conservative config? like max batch size 8, concurrency per-GPU 10?
03:47 Jamal Rivera: initial recommendation: for your mix start with max_batch=8, batch_timeout_ms=20, concurrency_target=10 per GPU. that limits queue buildup while still allowing batching to help.
04:01 Tom Becker: and for KV cache priming?
04:05 Jamal Rivera: prime the top 200 prefixes we see in the cold flows on startup, and keep a tiny background job refreshing them every 60s. that reduced misses in our internal tests.
04:14 Maria Gonzalez: how do we measure cold-path vs steady-state?
04:18 Alex Morgan: we can tag traces when the pod had <30s uptime or KV miss flag set; we'll provide a filter and a small heatmap to segment those.
04:27 Ibrahim Khan: any concerns with cost if we up min replicas?
04:30 Alex Morgan: yes there's a balance. increasing min replicas buys lower tail but costs more. Redwood Optimize can estimate unit economics for your traffic if you share sample week.
04:43 Rachel Lee: we'll share last week's traffic export. also curious about burst routing — if a region is saturated, does Redwood fallback to another model variant or region?
04:52 Jamal Rivera: policy-based routing exists — you can set fallbacks to cheaper quantized variants or to a different region. note though that cross-region adds latency.
05:03 Maria Gonzalez: we prefer same-region fallbacks and degraded-quality model if needed, over cross-region trips.
05:10 Alex Morgan: noted. we'll add a fallback playbook: local quantized variant first, then regional fallback if available, with thresholds.
05:20 Tom Becker: any security notes for priming? possibly those priming requests contain no PII but we want them to be marked and excluded from logs.
05:28 Jamal Rivera: yes mark them as synthetic and set retention to minimal. we support KMS encryption for payload at rest and transit; also audit logs can filter synthetic markers.
05:38 Maria Gonzalez: good. on the benchmark runs — we want deterministic seeds. you mentioned a microbench?
05:44 Alex Morgan: yep, Jamal will share a microbench harness (simple traffic generator) that we'll both run; it will reproduce cold path rates and token distribution.
05:53 Jamal Rivera: plan: 1) export the harness + instructions, 2) customer runs baseline, 3) we propose batch/concurrency matrix and they run the matrix, 4) Redwood analyzes and proposes final playbook.
06:06 Ibrahim Khan: curious about metrics frequency — currently our agent ships 60s windows; can you get per-10s?
06:12 Jamal Rivera: yes we can increase resolution but there's a small cost. for microbench runs we'll do high-res sampling.
06:20 Maria Gonzalez: ok excellent.
06:24 Alex Morgan: recap — short-term config changes (max_batch=8, timeout=20ms, concurrency_target=10), KV priming top-200 prefixes, run deterministic microbench, Redwood to deliver heatmaps + CSVs.
06:36 Tom Becker: timeline accept — we'll try to run microbench Friday.
06:40 Maria Gonzalez: final question — under dedicated pool, can we guarantee <200ms 95th?
06:46 Jamal Rivera: with dedicated warm GPUs and preloaded KV, yes that's realistic; cost will reflect reserved capacity. we'll model expected unit cost in the estimate.
06:57 Alex Morgan: great. i'll send notes and the files. Thanks all.
07:02 Maria Gonzalez: thanks everyone.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cache"), minor speaker attribution errors (Rachel sometimes labeled as "Speaker 4"), and some punctuation dropped.

Shared artifacts: https://redwood.app/heatmaps/ff-2025-10-28-coldpath-heatmap.csv (redwood export), microbench harness repo: https://git.redwoodinternal/bench/microbench (readme attached), playbook draft: https://redwood.app/playbooks/lumenix-coldpath-draft.pdf
